hypothesis: If Thompson is right, molecular-clock divergence times will show Perissodactyla and Leporidae sharing a more recent common ancestor with each other than Perissodactyla share with Artiodactyla or other ungulates, and than Leporidae share with other Rodentia.
pass_criterion: The claim is supported only if both inequalities hold in the TimeTree median divergence times. (1) T(Perissodactyla, Leporidae) is at least 5 Myr younger than T(Perissodactyla, Artiodactyla). (2) T(Perissodactyla, Leporidae) is at least 5 Myr younger than T(Leporidae, Rodentia). Each T is the median pairwise divergence time over representative species pairs. Representatives are Equus caballus, Ceratotherium simum, Tapirus terrestris, Oryctolagus cuniculus, Lepus europaeus, Bos taurus, Sus scrofa, Mus musculus, Rattus norvegicus and Cavia porcellus.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if T(Perissodactyla, Leporidae) is greater than or equal to T(Perissodactyla, Artiodactyla), or greater than or equal to T(Leporidae, Rodentia). Equivalently, it is refuted if the Perissodactyla+Leporidae pair is not recovered as a clade to the exclusion of Artiodactyla and non-lagomorph rodents. Either inequality failing is sufficient for refutation.
interpretation: Thompson inferred 'closer relationship' from skull-shape transformations (a uniform downward flexure of a rhinoceros skull gives a rabbit skull). I reinterpret it as phylogenetic relatedness, meaning recency of common ancestry. This is measured as pairwise divergence time in a time-calibrated molecular phylogeny. 'Other Ungulates' is operationalised as Artiodactyla, with Hyracoidea and Proboscidea as optional extra checks. 'Rest of the Rodentia' is operationalised as Rodentia (Mus, Rattus, Cavia). Modern phylogenomics places Lagomorpha with Rodentia in Glires (Euarchontoglires) and Perissodactyla with Artiodactyla in Laurasiatheria, so the claim is expected to fail. Morphological similarity is not tested here, only the stated relatedness inference.

dataset.name: TimeTree: The Timescale of Life (TimeTree 5)
dataset.why_it_fits: TimeTree gives median and confidence-interval divergence times between any two species or taxa, compiled from published molecular phylogenies. The planned fields are the pairwise divergence time (Mya) for each species pair, and the topology of the resulting tree for the ten listed representative species. These decide directly whether the Perissodactyla–Leporidae divergence is more recent than Perissodactyla–Artiodactyla and Leporidae–Rodentia.
